answer: Terrace the economy like a shale hillside: each identity earns standing only inside one narrow niche — one kind of work, one set of counterparties — and when several identities crowd the same terrace, that standing splits between them. A farm cloning itself into the most profitable niche dilutes its own clones to nothing, while spreading them across many terraces, like seed scattered by a gale, leaves each too shallow to take root. Copying stops paying, because every clone competes with its maker instead of with strangers.
